clue.text: Regularly jabbed old chaps in the tummy

indicators.note: regularly tells us to take every other letter of the word jabbed, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Some elderly men were poked in the stomach at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the even letters of 'jabbed', giving ABD.
explanation.definitionFit: Tummy is the informal word for the belly, the body's lower trunk.

clue.text: Topless demonstrator, one from Ambridge?

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, which in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: a demonstrator is one who marches in protest, a marcher

explanation.surface: A bare-chested protester turns out to come from a famous fictional village.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambridge is the village of The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap about a farming family; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archers family are the central household of the Ambridge radio soap, so one of them is an example.

clue.text: Unfold vacuous defensive gambit

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word defensive is emptied of its insides, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: a gambit is a ploy or tactical move

explanation.surface: A chess player unveils an empty-headed defensive opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy troops is to spread them out into position, to unfold them.

clue.text: Town boss supports males receiving assistance

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so it comes after
receiving means one word takes another inside it

parts.note: males are men
assistance is aid
a boss is the head of an organisation

explanation.surface: A local manager backs the men who are getting help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supports' in a down clue puts HEAD below M(AID)EN. Maidenhead is a town in Berkshire, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhead is a riverside town in Berkshire, England, so the plain definition is an example.

clue.text: Opera from Schumann or Mahler?

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Asks which of two great composers wrote a particular opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' picks the letters running across the end of Schumann and the start of Mahler; neither composer wrote the work, which is Bellini's.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's 1831 opera about a druid priestess, so it is an example of an opera.

clue.text: Pad out black leather 'older for gun

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a leather holder for a gun is a holster; the apostrophe in 'older shows the H dropped, as in Cockney speech, so the H goes from holster too

explanation.surface: A gunman stuffs out a black leather holster.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'older is mirrored in the gun holder, leaving OLSTER after B.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster an argument is to support or pad it out with more material.

clue.text: Lebedev working on summerhouse

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: on, in the sense of about or concerning, is RE

explanation.surface: A newspaper proprietor named Lebedev is busy working on a garden building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges LEBEDEV into BELVEDE; Evgeny Lebedev owns London newspapers, which makes the name look like the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a summerhouse or turret built to command a fine view.

clue.text: Mad, Charlie gets stuck in the gents

indicators.note: gets stuck in means one piece is lodged inside another

parts.note: the gents is a men's toilet, a loo in British slang
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie, furious, is trapped in the men's toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is American slang, from Spanish, for crazy or out of one's mind.

clue.text: Time published month long piece set in church

parts.note: a newspaper ran a story when it published it
Sept is the abbreviation for September

explanation.surface: A magazine printed a lengthy monthly feature about a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is the long transverse arm of a cross-shaped church, built across the nave.

clue.text: Yielded runs? England's opener got some spin

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: opener means the first letter, like a batting side's first batter

parts.note: a ball that got some spin turned

explanation.surface: A cricket report: did the runs come back as England's opening batter found turn?
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface misleads: 'opener' takes only E from England's.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment that yielded money returned it as profit, so both mean produced a gain.

clue.text: Cold day to be fooling around here in the Med

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
April Fools' Day falls on 1 April, written Apr I

explanation.surface: A chilly day of pranks on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The day for fooling around is April Fools' Day, the first of April, written APR I with the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, so it is a place in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Cattle run haphazardly, needing a prod?

indicators.note: haphazardly means in no fixed order, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Cattle stampeding wildly might need to be prodded back into line.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures cattle, but 'haphazardly' rearranges CATTLE RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reluctant is unwilling, needing urging or a prod before acting.

clue.text: Cleared English figure punching adult

indicators.note: punching means one piece is driven into another

parts.note: adult content is rated X, X-rated
a figure here is a number, one

explanation.surface: An English boxer is acquitted after hitting a grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exonerated is to be found not guilty, freed of blame.

clue.text: Emperor starts to talk sense about Russia

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A ruler begins talking sense about his country.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917.

clue.text: Dad's going out with reggae artist

indicators.note: going out suggests letters going out of order, with them all mixed together

parts.note: here the S counts as a letter, as in Dad is

explanation.surface: Father is dating a reggae musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going out with' rearranges DADS and REGGAE. Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter known for ballet dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French painter and sculptor, so he exemplifies an artist.

clue.text: Dish — for crooked farm labourer?

definitions.meaning: a dish of minced lamb under mashed potato
a pie belonging to the farmhand who carries a crook and tends sheep

explanation.surface: A meal intended for a dishonest farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests dishonest, but here it means carrying a crook, the hooked staff of a sheep herder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic British dish of minced lamb topped with mashed potato.

clue.text: Perhaps Elephant Man created by Stevenson beset by awful cramp

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so one piece goes around another
awful suggests the letters are in a terrible state and need rearranging

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the villain created by Robert Louis Stevenson in Jekyll and Hyde

explanation.surface: A deformed man in a famous story suffers from a nasty cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges CRAMP into PACRM, which surrounds HYDE. The surface evokes the Elephant Man, but 'Perhaps Elephant' is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is a thick-skinned mammal, and an elephant is the classic example.

clue.text: Adult daughter features in Prison Break caper

indicators.note: features in means appears inside another piece

parts.note: a prison break is an escape
A is the old film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up daughter appears in a jailbreak television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison Break' looks like the TV title, but is just an escape.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure, a caper.

clue.text: Secret gathering of Tories in the City of London

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London

indicators.note: gathering suggests the letters are collected and shuffled

explanation.surface: A clandestine meeting of Conservatives in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering of' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container; the City of London is the capital's financial district, whose postcode letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small inner circle, hence secret.

clue.text: Watch as snake shocked provincial N Americans here

indicators.note: shocked suggests letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Look out as a snake startles people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocked' rearranges WATCH AS SNAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saskatchewan is a prairie province of Canada, home to these North American provincials.

clue.text: A walk in the park for F1 driver?

definitions.meaning: a leisurely amble through a park
Lance ..., the Canadian Formula One driver

explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, and Lance Stroll is a Formula One driver.

clue.text: Smart wife cut up skirts

indicators.note: skirts means goes around the edges of another piece

parts.note: to cut up into strips is to shred

explanation.surface: A clever wife slashes up skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' is a verb meaning surrounds, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means sharp and astute, which is to say smart.

clue.text: American subaltern second to lose voice

parts.note: a subaltern is a junior officer such as a lieutenant, Lt

indicators.note: second to means the second letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A junior US officer is about to lose his singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second to' takes O, the second letter of 'lose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a vocal range, the lowest female or highest male voice.

clue.text: Cuddly Tom, smashing husband for the missus

indicators.note: smashing breaks the letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: A cuddly man named Tom makes a wonderful husband for his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' rearranges CUDDLY TOM. My old Dutch is Cockney rhyming slang (from duchess) for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: My old Dutch is an affectionate Cockney term for a man's wife, his missus.

clue.text: Section of lock in canal at Chester

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Part of a canal lock in the city of Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about canal locks, but the lock is the door kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is the bar or catch that forms part of a door lock.

clue.text: Newspaper article about English cheese

indicators.note: about means going around another piece

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
a is an article in grammar

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs an article on English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek cheese.

clue.text: Compact area outside Maine, fresh temperature

indicators.note: outside means one piece wraps around another

parts.note: fresh produce is green, not yet ripe or seasoned
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: A small region beyond Maine has a cool new temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compact' is the noun, a pact, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact is a formal agreement or treaty between parties.

clue.text: Good wander in wooded area

parts.note: to wander is to rove

explanation.surface: Have a nice ramble through the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove is a small wood or group of trees.

clue.text: Cry out suddenly "Alimony!"

definitions.meaning: alimony is what a former spouse claims, an ex's claim

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into EX and CLAIM: alimony is money a former partner claims.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, and alimony is an ex's claim.

clue.text: Ripped off covers from Honshu street light

indicators.note: covers from means the outside letters of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Removing street lighting from a Japanese island.
explanation.walkthrough: Honshu is the main island of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hustled is to be swindled, conned or ripped off.
